summary: Research complete with empirical build evidence. The arrow-only change (infix:30 -> infixr:25) has ZERO transitive parse impact: all 372 modules in the dependency cone built green (2013 jobs, 0 errors, warnings unchanged). One framing correction is load-bearing: iff sits at infix:30 (same level as the arrow) in Modal, LTL and Temporal, so moving the arrow alone inverts the arrow/iff binding; iff must move to infixr:20 in those three files. That combined variant also builds green. Working tree reverted clean.
decisions_made: Recommended edit set is 7 declaration lines plus 2 docstring precedence tables, not 4 lines: arrow infix:30 -> infixr:25 at Bimodal/Syntax/Formula.lean:101, LTL/Syntax/Formula.lean:209, Modal/Basic.lean:234, Temporal/Syntax/Formula.lean:169; PLUS iff infix:30 -> infixr:20 at LTL/Syntax/Formula.lean:210, Modal/Basic.lean:237, Temporal/Syntax/Formula.lean:170.

Task framing's premise that fork ordering is 36>35>30>20 holds only for the out-of-scope Propositional/Defs.lean; in three of the four in-scope files iff is at 30, not 20. Verified by rfl that leaving iff at 30 makes 'a -> b <-> c' parse as 'a -> (b <-> c)', inverting the standard binding and diverging from upstream.
Bimodal declares no iff notation at all, so it needs only the arrow edit.

Do NOT move and (36) or or (35). Their order relative to the arrow is preserved at either precedence and both already require parentheses as arrow arguments; build confirms zero impact. Defer or-at-35-vs-30 and the infix-to-infixr conversion for and/or to the notation-wide reconciliation.

Verification must use the targeted module list derived from Cslib.lean (372 modules), never a bare full lake build, which stalls on Propositional/Tableau/Intuitionistic/Scheme.lean. Expected signature: exit 0, 2013 jobs, 0 errors, 32 warnings.
Zero-debt: no sorry, no axiom, no BLOCKED recommendation needed. Pure notation-declaration edit with a green build already demonstrated.
dead_ends: Reasoning about parse impact from precedence arithmetic alone was insufficient: the infix:29 equivalence operator at Foundations/Logic/LogicalEquivalence.lean:33 looked like a genuine regression source (its args require prec >= 30, which an infixr:25 arrow fails), but every co-occurrence of it with an arrow in the four in-scope subtrees turned out to be a comment. Do not re-open this as a blocker.

Turnstile/derivation notations (Bimodal/ProofSystem/Derivation.lean:108, Temporal/ProofSystem/Derivation.lean:86) were suspected at-risk but use unannotated notation:50 arguments and are precedence-immune. Validity notations with annotated :50 args reject an arrow at 25, but already reject one at 30, so they are already parenthesized today. Neither is a regression.
The hypothesis that any existing site relies on the current non-associative parse is refuted by a full green build of the dependency cone; do not budget plan phases for fixing call sites.
